(青海时代新能源科技有限公司), located in Nanchuan Industrial Park, Xining Economic & Technological Development Zone, Qinghai. CATL has been on the Nanchuan site since 2012, with cumulative investment of ~RMB 5bn across ~2,000 mu of land. Per the Qinghai provincial government (Jan 2024), the base had built 8 production lines totalling 10.5 GWh/yr of power and energy-storage lithium batteries — hence status=operational and nameplate=10.5 GWh (capacity_ref_year 2024). Earlier plans (electric-vehicle-era reporting) referenced a phased build-out toward ~5-6 GWh, since exceeded. A 15 GWh technical-upgrade (技改) project was reported to be slated for production start around August 2025 (could raise eventual nameplate above 10.5 GWh, but sources do not clarify whether additive or a line replacement, so nameplate left at the confirmed 10.5 GWh). Separately, an electrode/cathode-processing (极片) project (RMB ~500m) broke ground 23 Jul 2025 targeting May 2026 completion — that is a materials line, not cell capacity. Qinghai is strategically chosen for salt-lake lithium resources and high-altitude/cold-dry climate that reportedly improves yield. Coordinates not found in a citable source, so left null; site is in Nanchuan Industrial Park, southern Xining (~36.5N, 101.8E, unverified). Note: a separately reported ~30 GWh sodium-ion pilot line in Xining, Qinghai appears attributable to BYD, not CATL, and was excluded. Lyten has scaled the site down from Northvolt's plans: ~15 GWh currently under construction with a path to 30+ GWh (vs Northvolt's 60 GWh), and ~1,000 jobs (vs 3,000). research_notes:
Britishvolt's planned lithium-ion EV cell gigafactory on the former coalyard/power-station site at Cambois, near Blyth, Northumberland (~250 acres, ~30km north of Newcastle). Planned nameplate ~30 GWh/yr built in three 10 GWh phases, with first production targeted around 2023-24 and full capacity by 2028; total project cost cited at £2.6bn-£3.8bn, up to ~3,000-8,000 jobs. Assets later bought out of administration by Australia's Recharge Industries (Feb 2023) and the site subsequently sold (2024) for redevelopment (reportedly a data centre campus). Status recorded as under_construction to reflect the furthest stage reached under Britishvolt, but the project is effectively defunct/cancelled. Cell format not reliably sourced; chemistry reported as li-ion for automotive (NMC-class) - treat as indicative. No reliable precise site coordinates found, left null to avoid guessing. Capacity figure (30 GWh, 3x10 GWh) corroborated across multiple news sources.

Battery cell gigafactory in the Espacio Navalmoral industrial park, Navalmoral de la Mata, Cáceres, Extremadura (part of Envision's planned Net Zero Industrial Park). Project branded VENERGY+. Groundbreaking ("first stone") ceremony held 8 July 2024 with Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez; 108 hectares reserved and site-preparation work initiated. Chemistry pivoted from the originally announced NMC to LFP (billed as one of Europe's first at-scale LFP producers). Phase-1 investment stated at >€1bn / ~$1.1bn, ~900 direct jobs.

I recorded nameplate_capacity_gwh=30 as the announced/eventual ambition, but the current realistic figure per the latest accounts is closer to ~10.6 GWh/yr — treat with caution.

A new environmental impact assessment was pending Extremadura regional approval as the 2023 declaration lapsed. Classified as under_construction given groundbreaking + site prep, but it may still be in late-permitting/early-works stage. start_year set to 2028 per latest guidance. chemistry: all-polymer lithium-ion (LFP cathode, resin-coated bipolar electrode)
research_notes:
APB's first ("1st") all-polymer battery plant, formally the APB Fukui Center Takefu Factory, in Echizen City, Fukui, Japan (address given in local press as Shoden-cho, Echizen City). Site area ~32,800 m2, floor area ~9,600 m2. Construction/acquisition 2020; opened 2021 with full "mass-production verification" from October 2021. This is a genuine cell manufacturer: it produces all-polymer battery cells, a next-generation lithium-ion design using resin-coated (gel-polymer) bipolar electrodes and an LFP cathode, targeted first at stationary storage (ESS) for buildings and renewable energy. Cell format recorded as pouch as the closest match — the true structure is a bipolar resin laminate, not a conventional wound/prismatic cell.

Capacity is uncertain and conflicting across sources. The Takefu line was to start at ~200 MWh/yr (0.2 GWh, captured in capacity_by_year_json for 2021) and expand to ~3 GWh/yr "within several years" via added equipment — recorded as the eventual nameplate, though never achieved. A separate, larger 8 GWh Japanese plant was planned for ~2026 but is a different (never-built) site, not this one; an earlier "1 GWh by 2023" target also appeared. Treat the 3 GWh nameplate as a plan, hence lower confidence.

Status: the plant did reach production (hence "operational"), but APB collapsed — funding withdrawn late 2024, all staff given retirement notices Feb 2025, and the Fukui District Court issued a bankruptcy order on 23 April 2025 (total debts ~JPY 3.485bn). The site is effectively defunct/idle as of 2026; no schema enum captures "closed". Parent listed as Sanyo Chemical Industries (largest shareholder / consolidating investor); APB also had many investors (Nissan licensed core IP, plus Obayashi, Toyota Tsusho, Yokogawa) but it is not a formal JV. Line 1 started shipping June 2009 at ~200,000 cells/yr; Line 2 came online June 2010 adding ~400,000 cells/yr for a Kusatsu total of ~600,000 cells/yr (sources: gs-yuasa.com press releases, Green Car Congress). These GWh values are my own calculation from sourced cell counts and the sourced LEV50 spec, hence lowered confidence. Chemistry: LEV50 is a manganese-based lithium-ion cell (lithium manganese oxide / NMC-type). Status: recorded operational as the LEJ Kusatsu site (GS Yuasa's lithium operations continue), but current 2024-2026 operating status and capacity were not confirmed by a recent source — i-MiEV production wound down around 2021, so present output may be reduced or repurposed. research_notes:
Third Ultium Cells plant, in Delta Township near Lansing, Michigan (~2.8m sq ft, $2.6bn). Announced Jan 2022 by the GM-LG Energy Solution JV (Ultium Cells LLC) with a stated ~50 GWh/yr full-production nameplate. In Dec 2024 GM agreed to sell its stake to LG Energy Solution; the deal closed in Q1 2025, so the site is now WHOLLY OWNED and operated by LG Energy Solution (no longer a JV — jv_partners left null; GM is the former JV partner). LG is repurposing the plant to build high-nickel NCMA pouch cells/modules for Toyota EVs assembled in the US.

STATUS: building is "nearing completion"; multiple mid-2026 reports state LG is targeting the START of mass production within 2026 (originally slated for late 2025). Since confirmed mass production had not yet begun as of the sources reviewed (mid-2026), recorded as under_construction rather than operational — this is the main uncertainty; it may already be ramping. start_year set to 2026 (target); could slip.

CAPACITY: sources conflict. Original 2022 JV announcement = 50 GWh/yr at full production (used as nameplate here). More recent trackers/press (2025-2026) cite ~40-41 GWh/yr for the plant as built ("will have an annual capacity of 41 GWh"; LG "planning to secure capacity of 40 GWh depending on demand"). No reliable phased ramp figures found, so capacity_by_year_json left null and capacity_ref_year null. Coordinates not sourced to a precise figure, left null (Delta Township, MI).

Note: this is DISTINCT from (a) LG's separate Holland, MI LFP-ESS plant, and (b) the separate ~$4.3bn Tesla-LG LFP prismatic plant planned in Lansing (production ~2027). This conversion is inferred, not a directly sourced GWh figure, and is a 2028 target (capacity_ref_year 2028), so confidence on the GWh number is low. Current 2025/2026 output is below this. If a GWh figure is not acceptable as derived, treat nameplate as null.
